classifiedFindings.title: migrate() accepts 1-wei slippage floors, so the story's 'no zero slippage floors' rule gives no sandwich protection (up to ~5% of a full-holder migration extracted on fork)
classifiedFindings.storyRef: story-121 Technical Details, migrate step 1: "Require ... and **all four** min amounts `> 0` (Configuration Safety: no zero slippage floors)." Concerns: previewMigrate exists so "the UI ... derive[s] slippage mins".
classifiedFindings.description: The only on-chain slippage rule is `minSUSDSOut, minPhUSDOut, amountSUSDSMin, amountPhUSDMin != 0` (L232). The story's stated purpose for that rule is to forbid unbounded slippage, but a floor of 1 wei is accepted and is economically identical to zero. The Router02 add (L245-246) is then priced entirely by the V2 pair's live reserves, which a searcher can move in the same block. The contract is user-facing (any BPT holder, via Etherscan or the not-yet-built phlimbo-ui modal), and the safe floors exist only as an off-chain convention (derive from previewMigrate). The Balancer leg is not the exposure: the holder owns ~100% of BPT and swaps are blocked once the pool is paused.
classifiedFindings.impact: Fork 26,303,097, whole-holder migrate (12,036.97 BPT -> 11,096.40 sUSDS + 13,145.69 phUSD, ~22,206 sUSDS of value) with 1-wei floors: a 10,000 sUSDS front-run/back-run sandwich of the V2 add costs the holder 1,101.79 sUSDS (~5.0%) and nets the attacker +893.92 sUSDS. A 2,000-token sandwich costs 54.55-74.80 sUSDS. With floors set 50 bp under an unmanipulated previewMigrate, every 2,000 and 10,000 front-run reverts, and the small ones that fit inside the band lose the attacker money. The protection therefore works when floors are meaningful, and the remaining exposure comes from user-chosen floors. That keeps this at Low: it is borderline user-input under C4 rules, but the story asserts the opposite property, the consuming UI does not exist yet, and BIP-928 makes this the only exit for a ~$25k position.
classifiedFindings.evidence: side-effects.json migrateForkResults.sandwichOfV2Add; test_r43_sandwich_oneWeiFloors and test_r43_sandwich_50bpFloors in work/test/audit-run43/BalancerLPMigratorRun43.fork.t.sol; log evidence/run43-tests.log
classifiedFindings.recommendation: Make it a binding requirement of the phlimbo-ui migration-modal story that the four floors come from previewMigrate(bpt), read when the user signs, minus an explicit bounded tolerance (for example <= 50 bp), and that a short deadline is used. Optionally, harden the contract by adding the pair's reserve ratio as a caller-supplied bound, or by requiring the two Router02 floors to be at least (1 - maxBps) of the Balancer outs times the pair ratio. At minimum, amend the NatSpec and story text so 'non-zero' is not presented as slippage protection.
classifiedFindings.dedupReasoning: Only candidate in the file (no intra-run duplicate). No ledger entry exists for src/periphery/BalancerLPMigrator.sol in either phStaging2 or yield-claim-nft; contract is new first-party (story-121), so cross-project analogues are related-not-duplicate. Evidence verified: test_r43_sandwich_oneWeiFloors and test_r43_sandwich_50bpFloors PASS in evidence/run43-tests.log (19/19).

classification.assetImpact: Value of a third-party BPT holder migrating via migrate(): the Router02 add is priced at live V2 reserves; with 1-wei floors a same-block sandwich extracted 1,101.79 sUSDS (~5.0%) of a ~22,206 sUSDS whole-holder migration on fork (test_r43_sandwich_oneWeiFloors PASS). With floors 50 bp under an unmanipulated previewMigrate every profitable sandwich reverts (test_r43_sandwich_50bpFloors PASS).
attackPath: 1. Holder submits migrate(bpt, ...) to the public mempool with token floors of 1 wei (passes the != 0 check at L232)
2. Searcher front-runs by swapping into the phUSD/sUSDS V2 pair, skewing reserves
3. Router02.addLiquidity (L245-246) deposits at the skewed ratio; amountSUSDSMin/amountPhUSDMin of 1 wei do not bind
4. Searcher back-runs; holder loses ~5% of position value, attacker nets ~894 sUSDS
classification.likelihood: low-to-medium - requires the caller to choose near-zero floors and use the public mempool; the only realistic victim set today is one EOA (0xc65f...e8db, ~all BPT) calling via Etherscan/direct because the phlimbo-ui modal that would derive floors from previewMigrate does not exist yet
classification.assumptions: Caller sets token floors materially below previewMigrate (e.g. 1 wei) and submits publicly. Contract behaves correctly when floors are meaningful.
classification.externalRequirements: Caller-chosen floors (user input); public-mempool submission; sufficient searcher capital to move a ~$45k-TVL V2 pair.

classifiedFindings.justification: Low (QA), not Medium. The loss is real and fork-proven, but it is gated entirely on a caller-supplied parameter: migrate() exposes four floors exactly like Uniswap Router02, and when set from previewMigrate with a bounded tolerance the protection works (50bp test). C4 treats choosing unsafe slippage parameters as user-input error, which caps this below Medium. It is kept at Low rather than invalid because (a) story-121 and the in-source NatSpec present the != 0 rule as Configuration Safety against zero slippage floors, a property that 1 wei does not deliver, (b) the victim is a third-party LP, not protocol-owned liquidity (story-121 Context: Sprint 34 migrated the protocol own LP; remaining BPT is held by third parties, largest 0xc65f...e8db), so the owner wont-fix stances on L-22/L-06/L-15 (keeper-chosen tolerance on POL, no user funds) inform risk appetite but do not transfer, and (c) the UI that would compute safe floors is a later, unbuilt phlimbo-ui story, so current callers are Etherscan/direct users with no floor guidance. Not an F-xx: the code faithfully implements the story letter (all four mins > 0, story step 1); the defect is that the story safety rationale overstates what that rule protects. Under Law 2 that is an unsafe-story flag, carried here as a recommendation to amend story/NatSpec and to bind the phlimbo-ui modal story to previewMigrate-derived floors, plus a one-line cross-reference in spec-conformance.md. Not an owner footgun (no owner action involved; contract has no owner).
classifiedFindings.humanReviewFlag: Borderline Low vs invalid (user-input). Raise to Medium only if the owner states that direct/Etherscan callers are an intended unattended path with no floor guidance before the UI ships. When filing, disclose ycn L-22/L-06/L-15 wont-fix (POL/keeper tolerance) and the related open ycn Q-24 (same >0-only floor mechanism on the operator escrow).
